heroHeadline: CNTE Teachers March to Zócalo; Metro Zócalo Station Suspended — 17 Days to World Cup
heroSubtitle: Mexico City's World Cup countdown entered its final 17-day stretch on May 25 with dual pressure: the CNTE teachers' union led a mass march from the Ángel de la Independencia to the Zócalo, joined by Pemex and CFE pensioners demanding restoration of energy-sector premium pensions — generating 36 total disruptions citywide. Simultaneously, Metro Zócalo/Tenochtitlán station was suspended and Perisur on Line 1 closed through May 31 in the final sprint to complete 20 station renovations before the June 11 opening match at Estadio Azteca. Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada declared 90% of all World Cup works complete on May 22, launched a mandatory Airbnb/Booking registry for 30,000+ short-term rentals, and confirmed 18 free fan zones across all 16 alcaldías. CDMX homicides continued declining — down 7% year-on-year in Jan–Apr 2026, the lowest level since 2022. Air quality orange alerts (May 18) marked the fifth ozone contingency of the pre-rainy season window; SEMARNAT and CDMX announced joint reforms to the Hoy No Circula and environmental contingency protocols.
